summary: 1939 Wisconsin standard tower in Douglas County, administered by the DNR; NHLR-registered 2017 and listed as standing; no staffing or access records found.

facts.design: 84-foot Wisconsin standard tower with external protected ladder

events.note: Registered August 28, 2017 as US 1244, WI 39; nominated by Tyler Bormann

evidence.supports: administered by the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources
84-foot Wisconsin standard tower with external protected ladder
evidence.quote: This 84-foot Wisconsin standard tower features an external protected ladder.

evidence.supports: register details block has no staffing or fire history

evidence.quote: Built in the 1930's and 1940's, the towers at the time were the front line to protect Wisconsin's forests.
In their heyday, the there were 119 towers staffed around Wisconsin.
Towers are typically around 100 feet tall

evidence.supports: DNR announced towers would be eliminated
evidence.quote: The DNR announced late last week the fire towers used to spot out of control fires were being eliminated.

evidence.supports: DNR notifying private landowners about options for towers and sites
evidence.quote: DNR is now in the process of notifying private landowners and presenting options for the future of the towers and the sites.

evidence.supports: FFLA lists Flannagan as standing, NHLR US 1244, WI 39
evidence.quote: Flannagan Douglas 46.58549 -91.93616 Tower Standing NHLR US 1244, WI 39

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 2015 WXPR report gives about 100 feet as typical for state towers; the register gives 84 feet for Flannagan itself. The statewide figure is not applied to this tower.

sources.title: State Fire Towers To Leave The Landscape

notes_for_editor: Register and FFLA agree on county, designation and standing. The 1939 build date and 84-foot height come from the register alone. No Flannagan-specific history, staffing, access or post-2015 status was found in two WebSearch queries and the sources read. The WXPR article is statewide context only and is not used as Flannagan's history. The 84 ft figure is overall tower height, not cab-floor height, so it was not entered as height_m.
